references.text: Describes the tenth plague where the Lord struck down all the firstborn in Egypt, which is the historical event referred to in verse 3:13.
God's command to consecrate all the firstborn to Him, both humans and animals, as a direct parallel to the dedication mentioned in Numbers 3:13.
Elaborates on the principle that all firstborn belong to the Lord and must be dedicated to Him, with the Exodus from Egypt as its background.
Confirms the commandment to give the firstborn of sons and livestock to the Lord.
Reiterates that all firstborn in Israel belong to the Lord and explains that the Levites were taken in place of the firstborn.
Shows how the Levites were chosen to replace the firstborn as the Lord's possession.
Confirms that the firstborn among livestock already belong to the Lord.
Command to consecrate all male firstborn of cattle and sheep to the Lord.
Refers to the law that every male firstborn shall be called holy to the Lord, as a fulfillment of the Old Testament commandment.
Mentions the assembly of the firstborn who are enrolled in heaven, as a spiritual application of the right of the firstborn.
